scope: Research readings of identified historical court orders. These are not a complete or continuously updated set of operative MDL orders.

briefs.title: AFFF / PFAS: removal and exposure allegations
briefs.summary: Judge Richard Mark Gergel addressed personal-injury pleadings that disclaimed AFFF exposure. Relying on State of Maryland v. 3M, the order described a plausible federal-officer removal basis where military-AFFF and other PFAS exposure could be intermingled. It contemplated later remand procedures and requested JPML transfer of related cases, including turnout-gear cases. It did not decide individual causation or damages.
briefs.mappingInsight: A shared PFAS product label alone does not establish membership in this MDL. Keep native transfer/master-docket identifiers and distinguish exposure allegations, removal arguments, and merits findings.
authorities: State of Maryland v. 3M, 130 F.4th 380 (4th Cir. 2025)
Dart Cherokee Basin Operating Co. v. Owens, 574 U.S. 81 (2014)

briefs.title: GLP-1 gastrointestinal injuries: direct filing and venue
briefs.order: Case Management Order 14 · Direct Filing Order
briefs.summary: Judge Karen Spencer Marston permitted qualifying actions to be filed directly in the Eastern District of Pennsylvania for coordinated pretrial proceedings. The order preserved jurisdiction and venue objections, Lexecon rights, and choice-of-law questions. A directly filed plaintiff had to designate an original venue and identify its basis. The court’s current directory describes disputed allegations of gastrointestinal injuries from GLP-1 medicines.
briefs.mappingInsight: A Pennsylvania docket does not establish Pennsylvania residence, injury location, governing law, or eventual trial venue. Those require the complaint’s designated-forum information and later orders.
authorities: Lexecon, Inc. v. Milberg Weiss Bershad Hynes & Lerach, 523 U.S. 26 (1998)

briefs.title: Bard implanted ports: master versus individual pleadings
briefs.summary: Judge David G. Campbell treated the master complaint as an administrative device, made operative for an individual plaintiff through incorporation in a short-form complaint. The order distinguished first-filed complaints from later master or short-form filings for limitations purposes. It preserved venue and jurisdiction objections and addressed transfer after pretrial proceedings. This 2023 order has later amendments listed by the court.
briefs.mappingInsight: Store master and member pleadings as separate records. A master filing date must not replace the individual case’s first filing date; a shared master complaint does not merge the underlying actions.
authorities: Lexecon, Inc. v. Milberg Weiss Bershad Hynes & Lerach, 523 U.S. 26 (1998)
Gelboim v. Bank of America Corp., 574 U.S. 405 (2015)

briefs.title: Proton-pump inhibitors: amendment deadlines and claim status
briefs.summary: Judge Claire C. Cecchi established a historical 30-day window for existing plaintiffs to seek leave to add specified GSK Consumer Healthcare defendants, requiring product-use evidence and good cause. The order did not grant amendments automatically, revive time-barred claims, alter limitations or repose periods, or change existing plaintiff-fact-sheet obligations.
briefs.mappingInsight: A deadline or amendment motion is a procedural event, not a merits outcome. Track parties and claims by dated pleadings instead of treating every named manufacturer as a defendant in every member case.
